finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set any price, including zero or negative, or a negative qty. The charge is then too small or negative, which is a refund or credit. Goods are obtained for little or nothing.

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, both taken directly from the request body
total is passed unvalidated to the payment charge
the charged amount is echoed back to the client

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup. No validation of price or qty for type, sign or integer-ness. No minimum on total. No middleware in this file checks the items. The safer /checkout-v2 handler in the same file shows the intended design, but the old route is still exposed. Whether req.user is authenticated is determined outside this file.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or sign/type validation (unlike /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14), and cart.js:6 charges that total, so any user who can reach the route (req.user is set elsewhere, and cart.js is the only file here) can charge zero or negative amounts.

verdict_facts.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no validation, cart.js:6 charges that total for any logged-in user, and nothing in cart.js (the only file) restricts it, unlike the catalog lookup and qty clamp in /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14.
